q: The heating effect of electric current has special applications in _____ appliances.
e: The heating effect of electric current has special applications in domestic appliances. Put industrial or medical in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: An electric light bulb consists of a glass bulb containing a _____ filament.
e: An electric light bulb consists of a glass bulb containing a tungsten filament. copper is not tungsten, and nichrome is not tungsten either. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: The tungsten filament has a high melting point of approximately _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: The tungsten filament has a high melting point of approximately 3000 ^°C. 1800 is not 3000, and 2500 is not 3000 either. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: A small amount of _____, an inert gas, is added to the light bulb after the air is removed.
e: A small amount of argon, an inert gas, is added to the light bulb after the air is removed. Put helium or neon in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: The tungsten filament emits white light at a temperature of _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: The tungsten filament emits white light at a temperature of 1800 ^°C. 3000 is not 1800, and 2500 is not 1800 either. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: Because of the inert gas, the light bulb can be used safely up to the temperature _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: Because of the inert gas, the light bulb can be used safely up to the temperature 2500 ^°C. 3000 is not 2500, and 1800 is not 2500 either. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: The inert gas in a light bulb reduces _____ of the filament.
e: The inert gas in a light bulb reduces evaporation of the filament. Put resistance or melting in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: In an electric iron, a mica sheet is wound around the _____ wire.
e: In an electric iron, a mica sheet is wound around the nichrome wire. tungsten and copper belong to other processes, not this nichrome case. Mica is a stable dielectric for precision capacitors that must not drift.

q: Mica is used in electric irons because it is a good electrical _____ and can withstand very high temperature.
e: Mica is used in electric irons because it is a good electrical insulator and can withstand very high temperature. conductor is not insulator, and semiconductor is not insulator either. Mica is a stable dielectric for precision capacitors that must not drift. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part.

q: The heating element in an electric iron is controlled by a _____ that switches the current on and off.
e: The heating element in an electric iron is controlled by a thermostat that switches the current on and off. fuse and resistor belong to other processes, not this thermostat case. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: An electric iron typically has an electric power of 750 - _____ W.
e: An electric iron typically has an electric power of 750 - 1000 W. Put 500 or 2000 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. An electric iron typically has an electric power of 750 - _____ W. 1000.

q: In an electric stove, a coil of nichrome wire is placed in the groove of the _____ material.
e: In an electric stove, a coil of nichrome wire is placed in the groove of the heat-resistant material. highly conductive is not heat-resistant, and magnetic is not heat-resistant either. Nichrome wire is placed in the groove of the _____ material. heat-resistant.

q: A fuse is a thin short wire of _____ alloy.
e: A fuse is a thin short wire of tin-lead alloy. Put copper-zinc or nickel-chrome in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: A fuse is used in electric circuits to prevent electrical appliances from being damaged if _____ current flows through them.
e: A fuse is used in electric circuits to prevent electrical appliances from being damaged if excessive current flows through them. alternating is not excessive, and direct is not excessive either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: The fuse wire is fitted in a glass tube, also known as a _____, or on a porcelain block.
e: The fuse wire is fitted in a glass tube, also known as a cartridge, or on a porcelain block. Put capacitor or coil in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

e: When a current greater than its rating flows, the fuse becomes so hot that it will melt and break the circuit. Put expand or vaporize in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: For an appliance rated as 700 W or less, a _____ A fuse should be fitted.

q: The voltage and the power of a simple light bulb are usually specified as 220 V and _____ W.
e: The voltage and the power of a simple light bulb are usually specified as 220 V and 60 W. 100 is not 60, and 15 is not 60 either. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: An electric stove has an electrical power ranging from 600 W to _____ W.
e: An electric stove has an electrical power ranging from 600 W to 2000 W. Put 1000 or 3000 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

e: According to Table 10.1, the electrical power of a laptop computer is 15-45 W. Put 100-250 or 40-100 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

q: According to Table 10.1, the electrical power of a radio and television receiver is approximately _____ W.
e: According to Table 10. 1, the electrical power of a radio and television receiver is approximately 150 W. Put 60 or 250 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

q: When a fuse melts and breaks the circuit, the current stops flowing and the electrical appliance is not _____.
e: When a fuse melts and breaks the circuit, the current stops flowing and the electrical appliance is not damaged. Put heated or charged in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: The heating effect of electric current is used in domestic appliances such as electric stoves, electric cookers, and electric _____.
e: The heating effect of electric current is used in domestic appliances such as electric stoves, electric cookers, and electric irons. fans is not irons, and motors is not irons either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: An electric kettle changes electrical energy into _____ energy.
e: An electric kettle changes electrical energy into heat energy. Put mechanical or sound in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy to provide electrical _____.
e: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy to provide electrical power. charge is not power, and resistance is not power either. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: An electric heating bag is an example of an appliance that uses the _____ effect of current.

q: A 13 A fuse should be fitted for appliances rated above _____ W.
